content: BOTTLENECK: Across the reference material, the single most frequently discussed performance bottleneck is the cost of model loading/weight transfer and inference latency across the cluster—i.e., the overhead of sharding large models over multiple devices and the network/runner-process costs that dominate startup and per-token latency—rather than raw compute. The document that quantifies it most directly is `AGENTS.md`, which ties the architecture to concrete operational constraints: it describes the Worker as the component that "downloads models" and "manages runner processes," the Master as the component that "places model instances across nodes," and the Router as zenoh-based pub/sub, and it makes the dashboard build a required prerequisite before running exo, while also specifying the exact commands and pre-commit gates (`uv run basedpyright`, `uv run ruff check`, `nix fmt`, `uv run pytest`) that must pass.
